text:
B: Hello. Erm, can you hear me?
A: Yeah. I'm Gemma.
B: I'm Kezia. Nice to meet you.
A: You too. Where are you?
B: Catford. South East London. Where are you?
A: Sutton-in-Ashfield. Notts.
B: Oh, okay. I don't think I've been. Is it near Nottingham?
A: Half hour. Nobody's been. It's fine.
B: Sorry. Erm, what do you do?
A: Manage a builders' merchants. Timber and plumbing stuff, mainly trade.
B: Oh, that sounds quite busy.
A: It is. Short-staffed, always. What about you?
B: I'm a teaching assistant. SEN, so I support two children with autism. In Year 3.
A: Is that hard?
B: Erm, sometimes. It's sort of about routine. If I keep everything the same, the days go well. If someone changes the timetable last minute, then it's, you know, a bad afternoon for everyone.
A: That sounds like my rotas. Except I'm the one changing them last minute.
B: Oh no.
A: Yeah. I'm not organised. I leave it till the night before. My staff love me.
B: I'm the opposite. I've got a planner with colour-coded stickers. Every week.
A: I saw your shelf, in the photo. All the folders labelled. I thought, she's sensible.
B: They're my resources for school. Visual timetables, social stories. I laminate them at home, I've got my own laminator.
A: Your own laminator. That's commitment.
B: It's quite cheap, actually. Is that okay, sorry, I'm talking a lot about work.
A: It's fine. More interesting than mine. What's a social story?
B: Erm, so if something's going to be different, like a fire drill, or a new teacher, I make a little story with pictures that explains what's going to happen, step by step. So it's not a shock. We read it a few times before. One of my boys, if we didn't do that for the fire drill, he'd be under the table for an hour.
A: That makes sense. Wish someone did that for head office restructures.
B: Ha. Yeah. What do you do when you're not at work?
A: Walk the dog. Read. Crime, mostly, I go through them quick. And there's a jigsaw on my table that's been there since Easter.
B: Since Easter? I'd have to finish it. It would bother me.
A: It bothers my husband. Doesn't bother me. Do you watch telly?
B: Bake Off. And Gogglebox. I just rewatch the same things, really. It's sort of relaxing, knowing what happens.
A: I watch quiz shows. Same reason, I think. You can just sit there.
B: Yeah. By Thursday I'm too knackered for anything new.
A: Thursday? Lucky. I'm knackered by Monday. Bacon cob van's shut Mondays, that's half of it.
B: Sorry, what's a cob?
A: Bread roll. A bacon roll.
B: Oh! We'd just say roll. Or a bap, maybe. My mum would—
